subject: general
question: ABC is an isosceles triangle in which AB = AC and ∠*BAC* = 50°. Side BC is extended to D. Find the measure of ∠*ACD*.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In an **isosceles triangle** with **AB = AC**, base angles ∠ABC and ∠ACB are equal.

Base angles = (180° − 50°) ÷ 2 = 65°.

The **exterior angle** ∠ACD is equal to the sum of the two opposite **interior angles**.

∠ACD = ∠BAC + ∠ABC = 50° + 65° = 115°.

**∴ The correct answer is 115°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **AB = AC** and ∠BAC = 50° in **▵ABC**.

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles in a **triangle** is 180°; **Linear pair** sum is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c2842ee79687b82aa3f9f3b6cf70788dfd57b08f9b6b0d5f62a4fc064b3c9db1.png] 

In **▵ABC**, since **AB = AC**:

⇒ ∠ABC = ∠ACB (Angles opposite to equal sides are equal)

⇒ ∠BAC + ∠ABC + ∠ACB = 180°

⇒ 50° + 2 × ∠ACB = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠ACB = 180° − 50° = 130°

⇒ ∠ACB = 65°

Side **BC** is extended to **D**, forming a **linear pair** at point **C**:

⇒ ∠ACB + ∠ACD = 180°

⇒ 65° + ∠ACD = 180°

⇒ ∠ACD = 180° − 65° = 115°

**∴ The correct answer is 115°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Exterior Angle Theorem

The exterior angle of a triangle is always equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles of the triangle.

Isosceles Triangle Property

If two sides of a triangle are equal, then the angles opposite to those sides are also equal.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all three interior angles of any triangle is always 180°.</p
